documentNotes.title: General instructions
documentNotes.statement:
General instructions: Observational Round: Planetarium (75 points)
 The Observational Round: Planetarium competition lasts for 45 minutes and is worth a total of 75 points.
 Before the exam

   • You must not open the marked envelope containing the problems before the signal indicating the
     beginning of the examination.
   • The beginning and end of the examination will be marked by a signal from you supervisors, they
     will also let you know when there are fifteen minutes before the end of the exam.
 During the exam

  1. We are going to present the Sky Observation Test by using a PPT presentation. The organizers in
     each country will project the presentation (PPT) by using a video beam or some similar system (e.g.
     TV). On the projection screen in front of the students a series of images with limited time will be
     projected. They look at the images and answer the questions in the Answer Sheets
  2. The Observational Round: Planetarium consists of 17 questions. On your desk you should find a
     marked envelope. Inside the envelope you will find:
        • Cover Sheet with question title, your student code, question code, and your name. Ex-
          ample: Observational Round: Planetarium GBR- 1 OR-2 John Smith (please make sure these
          are correct)
        • Question Sheets (marked Q)
        • Answer Sheets (marked A)
        • Working Sheets (marked W)
  3. Dedicated IOAA Answer Sheets (marked A) are provided for writing your answers. Enter the final
     answers into the appropriate boxes in the corresponding Answer Sheet. Please write only on the
     printed side of the sheet. Do not use the reverse side. Working Sheets (marked W) are provided
     for calculations.
  4. Use a black or blue pen for all answers and calculations, this will allow the markers to see your
     answers better after scanning. If you think you made a mistake cross it out.
  5. Use as many mathematical expressions as you think may help the graders to better understand
     your solutions. The graders may not understand your language. If it is necessary to explain some-
     thing in words, please use short phrases (if possible, in English).
  6. You are not allowed to leave your working desk without permission. If you need any assistance
     (malfunctioning calculator, need to visit a restroom, etc.), please put up your hand to signal the
     supervisor.
  7. At the end of the competition you must stop writing immediately. Sort your Answer Sheets and
     Working Sheets in order and leave them to be collected in their corresponding envelopes and ac-
     cording to the supervisor's instructions. You are not allowed to take any sheet of paper out of the
     examination area.

paper.caveat: The original projected slides are reproduced as static images in their source order. Their printed time limits and sequential star/object markers are retained; the page does not replay the timed presentation.

transcription.notes: Astra personally read all 42 prepared pages (2 question, 5 solution, 9 answer-sheet, 1 instructions, 25 slideshow pages). Original problem 1 comprises questions 1.1–1.17. Recovered the original projected slideshow, including all sequential star/object markers and slide 10 official correction M16(Aql) to M16(Ser). Printed answer-sheet/key disagreements retained: ecilptic/contellation, repeated C option in 1.15 versus E in key, Ameb/Murzim in key versus Arneb/Mirzam in question, and repeated image-9/stars wording in solution 17. No separate model checker. All 20 final no-snap crops personally viewed after upload. The 25-slide OOXML inventory contains no hidden slides, timing, transitions, audio/video or hyperlinks; all 24 note parts contain no text. Full-slide image crops intentionally preserve sky fields, printed captions, timing and marker order.

**(Image 1)** 2 mins (2+2+2 points)

1. Identify the drawn lines on the image:

**(Image 2)** 2 mins (3 points)

2. This image was taken from the town of Fada in Chad. What is the latitude of this place?

A. 10º

**B. 17º**

C. 22º

D. 33º

**(Image 3)** 3 mins (4 points)

3. Two of the following stars are transiting the meridian in the image. Tick the boxes to those stars.

| Arcturus | Mizar | Spica | Regulus |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | ✓ | ✓ |  |

**(No Image for questions 4, 5 and 6)** 8 mins

4. If the age of the Moon is 27.5 days, in which direction should we observe it and at what time? (2 points)

**A. Before sunrise to the east**

B. After sunset to the west

C. Close to zenith at sunrise

D. At 9 am rising in the East

5. Which of the Right Ascensions (RA) listed below will approximately coincide with the local meridian at Pune, India (74° E) on April 10 at 19:15 local time?. Select only one choice. (5 points)

A. 6 h

B. 7 h

**C. 8 h**

D. 9 h

E. 10 h

6. At what time during this night (April 10) would we find the Regulus [α Leo (RA = 10h 08m 22.3s, DEC = +11° 58' 02")] at its maximum altitude as seen from Pune, India? (4 points)

A. 18:00h

B. 19:00h

C. 20:00h

**D. 21:00h**

E. 22:00h

**(Image 4 for questions 7, 8, 9 and 10)**

The projected sky now corresponds to **–30º of latitude** (South) with **-74º longitude** (West).

7. Select the constellation pack that crosses the celestial equator on the image. 2 mins (3 points)

**A. Ori, Tau, Cet, Eri, Psc, Aqr, Aql, Ser**

**B.** Mic, Tau, Per, Cae, Mon, Aql, And, Ser

**C.** Gru, Tau, Cha, Ara, Aqr, Aql, And, Aps
